entries.text: Payload fairing. This cover protects the satellite during launch. Its two halves open and fall away when they are no longer needed.
Satellite. This satellite is the rocket’s cargo. Its solar panels are folded for the ride into space.
Upper stage. This smaller rocket sits above the main stage. Its engine helps carry the satellite toward its orbit.
Interstage. This hollow section joins two rocket stages. It surrounds the upper stage’s engine before the stages separate.
Rocket structure. The rocket has a strong, light structure. In this model, we open its outer skin to see the tanks inside.
Fuel tank. This tank holds liquid fuel. The engine uses fuel with an oxidizer to make hot gas.
Oxidizer tank. This tank holds liquid oxygen. It helps the fuel burn, even where there is no air.
Boosters. These two side rockets give an extra push at liftoff. They separate after their propellant is used up.
Main engines. These engines send hot gas down through their nozzles. That gives the rocket a push upward.
Two halves. The nose cone is made of two halves.
Pointed tip. The pointed tip cuts through the air.
Fairing skin. The smooth skin keeps the air flowing around it.
Seam. This line is where the two halves meet.
Satellite body. The box in the middle holds the instruments.
Solar wings. These wings make electricity from sunlight.
Antenna. The dish talks with stations on the ground.
Upper engine. This small engine fires again once in space.
Small tanks. These smaller tanks feed the upper engine.
Connector ring. This ring holds the two stages together.
Engine space. Inside is an empty space for the upper engine.
Ring frames. These rings keep the body round and stiff.
Stringers. These long beams run from top to bottom.
Outer skin. The thin skin is the outside wall of the rocket.
Separation line. This is where the rocket comes apart in flight.
Fuel chamber. Liquid fuel is stored in here.
Rounded dome. The rounded ends are the strongest shape.
Feed line. This pipe carries fuel down to the engines.
Oxidizer chamber. Liquid oxygen is kept cold in here.
Insulation. This layer keeps the cold liquid cold.
Booster case. The strong case holds the booster fuel.
Booster nozzle. Hot gas shoots out from here.
Bell nozzle. The bell shape speeds up the hot gas.
Combustion chamber. Fuel and oxidizer burn here.
Turbopump. The pump pushes propellant in very fast.
Gimbal mount. The engine can tilt to steer the rocket.
